questions.stem: A Spark join between a 2-billion-row fact table and a 500-row lookup table is slow because both sides are shuffled. What helps?

options.text: Collect the large table to the driver
Broadcast the small table so each executor has a copy and the large table isn't shuffled
Repartition the small table into 2,000 partitions

questions.explanation: A broadcast join sends the small table to every executor, avoiding a shuffle of the large one.

questions.stem: Which Fabric feature can speed up Spark queries by running them on a native vectorized engine, without code changes?
questions.explanation: The native execution engine runs supported Spark operations natively on a vectorized engine.

questions.stem: Queries on a large table always filter on EventDate. How can the table's layout reduce the data read?

options.text: Store it as one huge file
Z-order the table on EventDate with OPTIMIZE ZORDER BY, so filters skip files

questions.explanation: Z-ordering colocates rows with similar EventDate values, which tightens each file's min/max statistics so Spark skips files outside the filter.

questions.stem: A notebook reads the same expensive DataFrame in several later steps. What can avoid recomputing it each time?

options.text: Cache or persist the DataFrame after it's built

questions.explanation: Caching keeps the computed DataFrame in memory or on disk, so later actions reuse it.
